name: Mitokine Bio Science
old_description: Mitokine Bioscience was founded to impact diabetes care by developing a promising new treatment. That research is now being extended by Diamyd Medical in Sweden. Since opening in 2006, our company has maintained a commitment to innovative research that impacts medical problems and improves the daily lives of patients. Our current focus is providing information on the science of GABA and Alzheimer's disease.
about:
Mitokine Bio Science was founded in 2006 in Hancock, Maine, by Dr. Brooke Ligon, a board-certified neurologist with a doctorate in neuroscience from Tufts Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences. The company began with a mission to develop a novel treatment for diabetes, a research program that has since been taken forward by Diamyd Medical in Sweden.

Today the firm operates as a scientific information resource, concentrating on the biology of GABA and its relevance to Alzheimer’s disease. Dr. Ligon authors and curates the content, drawing on her clinical and research background. No manufacturing facility, production volumes, or part numbers are disclosed; the output is published research summaries and educational material rather than physical goods.

The organization’s work is linked to several academic and philanthropic institutions, including Tufts Medical Center’s Department of Surgery, Molecular Cardiology Research Institute, and GRASP Center, as well as Tufts University’s Neuroscience Department and Vice Provost Office for Industry Collaboration. The Kyle Family Foundation, a charitable entity that supports medical research, is also noted as a connected party. These relationships suggest an audience of researchers, clinicians, and research-funding organizations.

Mitokine states that its distinguishing feature is a sustained commitment to innovative research that addresses medical problems and improves patients’ daily lives. The transition from an internal diabetes drug program to an open information platform on GABA and neurodegeneration reflects that stated purpose.
